paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : MMLU Pro confidence vs. accuracy
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and three accuracy metrics—Final Accuracy, $\Delta$ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy. The x-axis represents "Initial Confidence" on a linear scale, ranging from 0.81 to 0.99, with numeric tick labels generally spaced at intervals of 0.01, although the label for 0.83 is omitted. The y-axis represents "Accuracy" on a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels spaced at intervals of 0.2. All three lines feature vertical error bars at each plotted data point. The "Final Accuracy" line is depicted as a solid blue line with circular markers, beginning at its highest point of 1.0 at x=0.81, dipping to approximately 0.91 at x=0.82, and fluctuating predominantly between 0.87 and 0.98 across the remainder of the axis, with a notable local peak of roughly 0.98 at x=0.90 and a low point of approximately 0.87 at x=0.95 before concluding at roughly 0.98 at x=0.99. The "$\Delta$ Accuracy" line is shown as a dashed orange line with diamond markers, starting at roughly 0.46 at x=0.81 and exhibiting a fluctuating but overall declining trend; it drops to local minimums of roughly 0.15 at both x=0.86 and x=0.89, rises to minor local peaks around 0.38 at x=0.88 and 0.30 at x=0.93, and ultimately ends at its lowest value of approximately 0.04 at x=0.99. The "Initial Accuracy" line is represented by a dash-dot green line with square markers, starting at approximately 0.54 at x=0.81 and demonstrating a general upward trend alongside intermediate fluctuations; it shows local peaks of roughly 0.76 at x=0.86 and x=0.89, and dips to approximately 0.52 at x=0.82 and 0.58 at x=0.88, before rising to end at its highest value of approximately 0.94 at x=0.99.
